answer: Coordination Cost Bridge.** Each agent identity must publish a signed sonnet-like hash puzzle: a fixed-length commitment whose solution depends on the previous epoch’s global coordination graph. To join a coalition, an identity must bridge its puzzle to every co-member, paying a routing fee proportional to pairwise distance in that graph. The rule: coalitions pay the sum of all bridge edges, recomputed each epoch from a public fable of prior edge costs.
